guard: a spawn or a resume may arm the event plane of the agent it names and no other, over both ACL fields and at every seam, and the wildcard form is deliberately left to ordinary ACL authority
why: An event channel carries a session's tool inputs and outputs verbatim. On a static mesh there is
no ledger, so a caller-supplied allowSubscribe/allowPublish is attenuated by nothing at all, and a
resume document is admin-supplied JSON that re-arms a managed row which `renewManagedStaticCred`
then re-mints a credential out of at half TTL.
E1 removes the rule's predicate. E2 leaves the rule but narrows its INPUT to one of the two ACL
fields, which is the shape a refactor produces and which E1 cannot distinguish. E3 goes the other
way and makes the rule catch MORE than it claims to, which is the only way to show the
stated-limit cell is an assertion rather than a sentence. E4 removes the rule from the RESUME door
while leaving it on the spawn door, which is the state this PR was in when a security review found
it: every spawn cell stayed green and a foreign concrete channel was mintable through an inventory.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY. The suite imports the manager by relative source path (../src/manager.js), so
the mutated file is the file that runs and there is no build in the command. Its package-name
imports are core's eventChannel/eventChannelPrincipal, which the cells compare the manager
AGAINST; no mutation below replaces them, so a kill cannot come from moving both sides.

mutations.name: E1 the rule finds nothing foreign, ever
mutations.find: return p !== null && !(p.owner === owner && p.actor === actor);
mutations.expectRed: a spawn asking for ANOTHER agent's event channel to READ is refused
mutations.cell: a spawn asking for ANOTHER agent's event channel to READ is refused
mutations.note: The rule deleted at its predicate rather than at a call site, so every surrounding throw and message survives and cannot pass a cell by itself.

mutations.name: E2 the spawn seam reads the read-set only, and forgets the post-set
mutations.expectRed: a spawn asking to POST to another agent's event channel is refused too
mutations.cell: a spawn asking to POST to another agent's event channel is refused too
mutations.note: The half-fence. It reads as the obvious one, because read amplification is the risk people name first, and it leaves a caller able to mint publish rights onto another agent's plane, which is forgery rather than eavesdropping. E1 cannot tell this mutant from a healthy tree.

mutations.name: E3 the rule catches the wildcard form too, which it does not claim to
mutations.replace: const p = eventChannelPrincipal(ch) ?? (ch.startsWith("events.") ? { owner: "", actor: "" } : null);
mutations.expectRed: a WILDCARD event pattern is NOT refused by this rule
mutations.cell: a WILDCARD event pattern is NOT refused by this rule
mutations.note: The limit asserted from the other side. Without it, the cell recording the gap is satisfied by any tree including one that had quietly closed it, and the comment describing the limit is a sentence nobody tests.

mutations.name: E4 the rule covers the spawn door but not the resume door
mutations.expectRed: an inventory naming ANOTHER agent's event channel is refused at the resume door
mutations.cell: an inventory naming ANOTHER agent's event channel is refused at the resume door
mutations.note: Not an invented mutant: this is exactly the state the change was in when a security review reproduced a foreign concrete event channel being minted through an admin inventory plus one credential renewal. Every spawn cell stays green under it, which is why it needed its own cell rather than trust in the existing ones.
